demo.title: Asking is not the same as being allowed.
demo.intro: An illustration that runs in your browser and is connected to nothing. Start the request and watch where it stops. It will not go any further until you approve that exact revision yourself.
demo.approvalLabel: Your approval covers only the target, operation and revision shown above.
demo.halt: Stopped here. The flow is waiting for a human decision and will not continue on its own.
demo.legend: Refused · Waiting for a person · Passed
demo.initial: DENIED · production/payment-api sits outside staging/*, and nobody has approved it.
demo.denied: DENIED · This action is outside the standing scope, or it no longer matches the approval on file. It stops here for a person to look at.
demo.approved: APPROVED · Your approval is bound to the target, operation and revision shown, so the request clears the gate and the flow runs to the end. Nothing real was touched.
demo.allowed: ALLOWED · This exact request now has authority, so the flow runs to the end. Nothing real was touched.
demo.invalidated: APPROVAL REVOKED · The request changed, so the previous approval is void — even if you set the values back to what they were.
demo.evidence: Illustrative evidence: identity workflow-agent-17, the target and revision, the policy decision, and what the approval actually covered. After a real action you still compare what happened against what was approved, and reconcile any difference.
demo.static: A restart of production/payment-api by workflow-agent-17, which is authorized only for staging/*, is refused. A human approval naming that target, the restart operation and revision 182 permits that one request and nothing else. Identity and permissions come from the execution layer, never from what the model claims about itself.

home.eyebrow: FACTOR IO / KUBERNETES · INFRASTRUCTURE · ENTERPRISE AI
home.headline: Kubernetes, infrastructure, and the AI that runs on it.
home.lede: Factor IO builds the platform layer that any enterprise workload can run on. AI is the workload at the front of the queue right now, and it is our specialisation — model serving, knowledge systems, and the governance that decides what AI is allowed to do. The platform underneath is what makes it survivable.

sections.title: The platform is general. The specialisation is not.
sections.body: Kubernetes and the infrastructure under it are built to carry whatever the business needs to run — applications, data, batch work, and the workload nobody has chosen yet. That generality is the point: a platform built around one workload has to be rebuilt when the next one arrives. What we go deep on today is AI, because AI is what is arriving. Both statements matter and they are not the same claim. The platform is where the durability is. AI is where the specialisation is.

sections.title: Plan for the day people start relying on it.
sections.body: We work through these questions during design. Then we test against agreed requirements and prepare your team to operate the system. If you already have a pilot, we can assess what it needs before it goes into production.

items.title: Who can access the data?
items.body: Access follows the roles and approvals your organisation already uses. It gets settled during design, not after the system is live.

items.title: How will you check the answers?
items.body: Results are tested against requirements you agreed, so a reviewer can check the work rather than having to trust it.

items.title: What happens when something fails?
items.body: Failure handling is part of the design: what stops, what is retried, and who gets told about it.

items.title: Who will look after the system?
items.body: Your team. We prepare them to operate it, and the procedures are written down before handover.

sections.title: Four services, scoped to what you already run.
sections.body: Each one can be a standalone engagement or a stage of a larger delivery. The platform work comes first because everything else sits on it. We agree responsibilities and acceptance criteria before implementation begins.

items.title: Kubernetes and infrastructure
items.body: We design and deliver the platform your applications need, including Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure. It is built to carry whatever you run on it rather than one workload in particular. Capacity, recovery, upgrades and day-to-day ownership are part of the design. We start with the systems you already run.

items.title: Enterprise AI
items.body: Tell us what you want AI to do for the business. We help define the scope, choose an approach and build it into your existing environment. Our work covers model selection, system integration, testing and deployment.

items.title: Knowledge systems
items.body: Make your organisation's information useful to AI. We help establish which sources to trust, who can access them and how to keep them current. That gives the search and answer system a clear set of requirements to work against.

items.title: AI governance
items.body: Decide what AI may do on its own and when a person needs to approve the next step. We design controls around those decisions, including access, review and how to handle failures. The scope includes how those controls will be tested.

sections.title: An instruction is a request. A permission is a fact.
sections.body: This is what the AI governance service produces: a decision made before the action runs, not a rule written into a prompt and hoped for. The illustration below is the shape of that control, not a product you buy.

sections.title: Send people the cases that genuinely need a person.
sections.body: AI handles the volume; people handle the judgment. What gets escalated is written down as a rule during design, so nobody is asked to trust a confidence score without seeing the evidence behind it.

items.title: Normal result
items.body: Runs under the policy already approved.

items.title: High-value transaction
items.body: Always goes to a person.

items.title: Missing evidence or conflicting data
items.body: Stops and asks someone accountable.

items.title: Low confidence
items.body: Escalates instead of guessing.

items.title: Against policy
items.body: Blocked, then routed to review.

items.title: Wide blast radius
items.body: Needs explicit approval first.

sections.title: Keep model choice separate from authority.
sections.body: Agents can run on local, enterprise-hosted or frontier models. Identity, authorization, scope, approval, tool access, state, audit and reconciliation are checked before any of them reach your systems. Choosing a different model does not change who is allowed to do what.

sections.title: AI workflows need maintenance, not just a launch.
sections.body: Review the corrections people made, the outputs they rejected, the escalations and exceptions, how long things take and what changed in the data and the business rules. AI can propose improvements, but every change is tested, reviewed and released as a controlled revision. Production policy never changes quietly. Ongoing support is agreed separately, per project.

sections.title: Architecture, integration and a team that can carry it.
sections.body: The aim is a system your own team can understand, operate and improve after we hand it over.

On your project, your interests are the ones we protect: recommendations follow your requirements and constraints, we say when a simpler or cheaper option would serve you better, and we disclose any relationship that could bear on our advice before it bears on a decision. We are not a reseller or a formally certified partner, and the scope and responsibilities of every engagement are agreed with you directly.
